subject: Getting effective sample size from null model?

messages.author: 3242b567895bad92
messages.subject: Getting effective sample size from null model?
parts:
I'm trying to compute a Bayes factor between two models. The first model is just a null model with only an intercept:

# Set prior on intercept -------------------------
m0priors = c(prior(cauchy(0,10), class = "Intercept"))

# Fit null model with only intercept
m0 <- brm_multiple(DV ~ 1,family="bernoulli",
                   data=data3.short,
                   save_all_pars=TRUE,
                   prior=m0priors,
                   iter=20000)
summary(m0)

The second model adds a single predictor:

# Set prior on intercept and on regression ------------------------
# Use only standardized variable so can make reasonable choices on b priors
m1priors = c(prior(cauchy(0, 10), class = "Intercept"),
           prior(cauchy(0, 2.5), class = "b"))

# Fit model with gender cognition
m1 <- brm_multiple(DV ~ IV,family="bernoulli",
                   data=data3.short,
                   save_all_pars=TRUE,
                   prior=m1priors,
                   iter=20000)
summary(m1)

And I'm trying to compute the Bayes factor via the bridge_sampler package. While I'm not getting this issue with M1, for M1 I'm getting the following error:

> bridge_m0 <- bridgesampling::bridge_sampler(m0)
Iteration: 1
Iteration: 2
Iteration: 3
Warning message:
effective sample size cannot be calculated, has been replaced by number of samples. 

Has anybody had similar issues? At first I thought the issue might be with using "brm_multiple", but the fact that no warning comes up for M1 leads me to believe this explanation isn't likely. Might it be something about the fact that the model has no predictors?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Getting effective sample size from null model?
parts:
Since this is a very simple model comparion, you can also use a savage-dickey ratio as implemented in the hypothesis() method for the computation of Bayes factors.
See https://rpubs.com/lindeloev/bayes_factors for details.

However, in this case, you should **not** use a cauchy prior, but something with smaller tails such as student-t with >= 3 dfs or a normal distribution.

Agreed - I should have called the message a warning, not an error. The bayes factor > 10, and I was a bit surprised by that. I was expecting something more in the range 6 or so.
